title: Approve vaginal pH modulation for on-demand non-hormonal contraception

concept.text: Enable woman-controlled pregnancy prevention through a non-hormonal vaginal pH-modulating product used around intercourse. Phexxi achieved approval, but its efficacy is substantially below long-acting contraception. Proposed completion test: FDA approval specifically for on-demand pregnancy prevention, based on a phase 3 study measuring cumulative pregnancy incidence over seven menstrual cycles and reviewing local and urinary safety. Test set by: FDA; its review accepted a seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate of 13.7% with a 95% confidence interval of 10.0–17.5%. This was not a Pearl Index below 2. Reported achieved: FDA approved Phexxi on 22 May 2020. Sources given: [FDA Phexxi approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2020/208352Orig1s000ltr.pdf) ; [FDA multidisciplinary efficacy and safety review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2020/208352Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf).

page.title: First FDA-approved contraceptive acting by vaginal pH modulation
page.definition: Phexxi is the first nonhormonal contraceptive approved by FDA that acts by maintaining vaginal acidity in the presence of semen. In laboratory tests the gel kept pH between 3.5 and 4.5. Tests after intercourse found reduced sperm movement. A fresh dose is applied vaginally immediately before or up to one hour before each act of intercourse.

goal.need: In 2019, 41.6% of US pregnancies were unintended. Women who cannot tolerate hormones or have a medical reason to avoid them can use a vaginal gel without nonoxynol-9, the spermicide in other contraceptive gels. They can apply it themselves when needed, which may suit women who have intercourse infrequently. Each act requires a fresh dose. Pregnancy rates are in the range seen with nonoxynol-9 spermicides and higher than with hormonal methods.

statements.quote: The Panel recommends additional development of female contraceptive modalities that are delivered to the reproductive tract
statements.context: The recommendation concerns blocking egg or sperm function within the female reproductive tract on demand.

statements.quote: we intend to seek regulatory approval for product labeling stating Phexxi can be used on-demand, immediately before or up to one hour before intercourse.
statements.context: The company's annual report for 2019 describes its intended contraceptive indication.

completion.title: FDA approves the first contraceptive that acts by vaginal pH modulation.
completion.criterion: FDA grants an effective approval for at least one contraceptive whose approved labeling indicates prevention of pregnancy and identifies maintenance of an acidic vaginal pH in the presence of semen, with reduced sperm motility, as contributing to its contraceptive action.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.105(a) and (c), approval letter and prescribing information for NDA 208352.
completion.threshold_quote: FDA will approve an NDA after it determines that the drug meets the statutory standards for safety and effectiveness, manufacturing and controls, and labeling
completion.basis: FDA approved Phexxi on May 22, 2020, for on-demand prevention of pregnancy. The original label identifies a pH-lowering effect and reduced sperm motility. The same formulation had received clearance as a personal lubricant in 2004. The 21% upper confidence bound was the prespecified efficacy target for AMPOWER.

milestones.title: A vaginal gel keeps a semen mixture below about pH 5 in a laboratory test.
milestones.criterion: In a laboratory assay that mixes the gel directly with human semen from more than one donor, the mixture stays below about pH 5 at a stated gel:semen ratio. The report states the ratio, the number of donors and the measured pH.
milestones.set_by: Rush-Presbyterian-St. Luke's Medical Center inventors, formulation target and laboratory assay in US patent 6,706,276, claim 1 and Example 10.
milestones.threshold_quote: wherein the composition maintains an acidic vaginal pH of less than about 5 in the presence of semen ejaculated from the male

milestones.title: FDA permits a 14-day vaginal-gel safety study in women to proceed.
milestones.criterion: FDA reviews, under an investigational new drug application for the gel, the protocol of a study of at least 14 days of vaginal use in women and determines that it is safe to proceed, on nonclinical evidence that includes a vaginal irritation study in animals. Submission of the application without a recorded determination is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, regulatory history for IND 64623 reproduced in the NDA 208352 multidisciplinary review.
milestones.threshold_quote: Both study protocols were reviewed and determined to be safe to proceed.

milestones.title: A vaginal gel yields fewer than one forward-moving sperm per microscope field in a postcoital test.
milestones.criterion: In a postcoital test in women protected from pregnancy, midcycle cervical mucus sampled after intercourse with the gel applied beforehand contains, as the mean across women, fewer than one progressively motile (forward-moving) sperm per high-power microscope field, averaged across the fields examined, and the same women exceed that cutoff in a cycle without gel.
milestones.set_by: ACIDFORM postcoital-study investigators; the study-specific cutoff is restated by co-investigator Christine K. Mauck and Kathleen L. Vincent in their 2020 account.
milestones.threshold_quote: the cut-off of less than one PMS/HPF in the later Acidform study

milestones.title: A vaginal gel's seven-cycle pregnancy rate has an upper 95% confidence limit of at most 21%.
milestones.criterion: In a phase 3 trial, women aged 18–35 are instructed to apply the gel before each act of vaginal intercourse. The upper 95% confidence limit of the Kaplan–Meier seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate under typical use is at most 21%. Qualifying cycles last 21–35 days, include recorded vaginal intercourse and involve no backup or emergency contraception. The primary analysis also includes eligible women who conceive between enrollment and less than eight days after final gel use. Report the numbers of women, qualifying cycles and on-treatment pregnancies.
milestones.set_by: Evofem, Inc., AMPOWER protocol AMP002, registered as NCT03243305, version 4 dated 1 November 2017, sections 9.2 and 9.8.
milestones.threshold_quote: the upper limit of the 95% CI of the cumulative seven-cycle pregnancy rate is less than or equal to 21%.

results.finding: Acidform Gel: CONRAD submitted one IND (64,623).
results.detail: The rabbit sample size for the 10-day study is unstated. FDA’s later pre-IND agreement that additional nonclinical studies were unnecessary does not establish clearance of the specified protocol.
results.quote:
• April 29 – Submission of IND 64,623 for Acidform Gel as vaginal contraceptive gel by 
CONRAD.

results.finding: PHEXXI in AMP002 (1,183 women analyzed): the upper 95% confidence limit for seven-cycle typical-use pregnancy was 17.5%.
results.detail: The analysis plan allowed inclusion based on conception after enrollment and within seven days of last use. The reported primary estimate used 101 pregnancies from cycles 1–7. FDA identified five additional pregnancies in cycle 8 within that post-use window.
results.quote:
The seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate in the mITT population estimated by the Kaplan-
Meier method is 13.7% (95% CI: 10.0%, 17.5%) (Table 9).

results.finding: ACIDFORM yielded a mean of 0.19 progressively motile sperm at 0–30 minutes before intercourse in a crossover study enrolling 20 sterilized women.
results.detail: The excerpt gives 20 as the enrollment count and leaves the number contributing to each mean unspecified.
results.quote: ACIDFORM or N-9 product administered 0-30 min precoitus or ACIDFORM given 8-10 h precoitus significantly reduced the mean number of progressively motile sperm compared to control cycles (0.19, 0.07, 0.75 vs. 17.94, respectively, p<.05, Wilcoxon test).

results.finding: PHEXXI lowered pH in vitro. The label gives no sample size or measured pH.
results.quote:
In vitro studies showed that a pH lowering effect and sperm motility reduction contribute to the activity 
of PHEXXI in the vagina.

results.finding: PHEXXI AMP002 (1,183 women) had a seven-cycle typical-use pregnancy rate with an upper 95% confidence limit of 17.5%.
results.detail: The label does not say whether the primary analysis included eligible women who conceived between enrollment and less than eight days after final gel use.
results.quote:
The 7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 13.7% (95% 
CI: 10.0%, 17.5%), excluding cycles with back-up contraception, cycles <21 days or >35 days in 
length and cycles in which no intercourse was reported.

results.finding: Phexxi in 1,114 women in AMPOWER had a seven-cycle typical-use pregnancy rate with an upper 95% confidence limit of 17.5%.
results.detail: The paper reports more than 24,000 qualifying cycles and separately reports 24,289 acts of intercourse within qualifying cycles. It gives no exact qualifying-cycle count.
results.quote: The seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy percentage was 13.7% [95% confidence interval (CI): 10.0%–17.5%], meeting the prespecified primary endpoint of having the upper bound 95% CI ≤ 21%.

results.finding: In the Phexxi trial (1,183 women), the upper 95% confidence limit for the seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 17.5%.
results.quote:
The 
7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 13.7% (95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 10.0%, 17.5%), 
excluding cycles < 21 days or > 35 days in length, cycles with back-up contraception, and cycles 
in which no intercourse was reported.

results.finding: Vaginal trapping gel mixed with semen from five donors yielded a mean pH of 4.45.
results.detail: Table XII reports the exact mean. The accompanying text describes it as below pH 4.5.
results.quote:
For instance, when 1 part gel was mixed with 2 parts semen, the pH remained below 4.5 with the inventive gel but was
almost 6.0 with Aci-Jel™.

results.finding: Vaginal gel without nonoxynol-9 had a mean irritation score of 5.3 in 10 rabbits.
results.detail: The investigators considered the formulations acceptable for clinical evaluation. The exact mean score appears in Table II.

results.finding: In 20 women, ACIDFORM applied 0–30 minutes before intercourse yielded a mean of 0.19 progressively motile sperm per high-power field.
FDA approved PHEXX vaginal gel in 2020 for pregnancy prevention with a labeled pH-based mechanism.
results.detail: The approval applies to one product. The label does not give sample sizes for the mechanism studies.
